derived_from.operation: image edit: lower the moon in the panorama so it clears the top HUD in the center camera and retain the floor contact band.

purpose: Center-camera layout correction candidate for Suzaku; exact aspect ratio is close to 640x224. Concept only, not native hardware art.
prompt: Refine the vertical composition of this original AI-generated wide pixel-art Japanese castle fighting-game stage. Keep the same 2:1 canvas, palette mood, castle centered horizontally, moon horizontally about two-thirds of the panorama, clouds, mountains, railings, lanterns, and stone floor. The image will later be fit to a 640x224 world by preserving its full width and cropping the lower part; therefore place the moon center at about 24% of the source canvas height from the top (around y=245 on a 1024-pixel-tall canvas), rather than near the top fifth. This should put the moon lower in the playable image, mostly beneath a fixed HUD occupying y=0..55, with its center near playfield y=78 after hardware framing. Keep the castle's main spire center near y=250 so it remains visible in the camera's central view. Keep the floor contact zone near y=560 of the source (about playfield y=175 after width scaling), leaving clear room for fighters' feet at y=200. Preserve crisp hand-clustered 16-bit pixel-art, strong readable silhouettes, selective cloud highlights, and a restrained warm lantern glow. No smooth gradients, photo textures, text, fighters, UI, or new objects. This is a precise layout correction; do not change the scene design.
